items.title: Mike Vax interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 29, 2022
items.q: Bud Brisbois did play some lead but a lot of the time on a lot of recordings he was the high note player

ctx.x: Well it’s a lot of pressure. You know I mean and it’s interesting that I was put on lead trumpet two days before the “Redlands” album. The lead trumpet player before me, Jim Kartchner, had a brain tumor and didn’t know it and he was having all kinds of chop problems. And a few days before, you know “Redlands” was the first album on Creative World. I mean Stan was really nervous about this. You know it was the first album away from Capitol on his own label. And so Jim just said, “I don’t want to mess up the album,…

do I get — and some of the guys in the band said, “You know Vax can handle it.” And so this is like two days before and I get called down to breakfast and Stan had been really nervous about this whole thing and was thinking about using big name guys from L.A. that had been on the band before. And Willie Maiden, rest his soul, said to Stan, “These young kids are playing your music as good as anybody ever has and if you use any ringers you can’t record my music.” He was adamant about, you’ve always used your road…

like yeah, this is really cool. And, but the consistency has to be there or the time has to be there, and the sound has to be right to carry over the band, you know, because a lot of times the lead trumpet has the melody. It’s the responsibility.
